name: Pane
text: Mocked API responses risk providing a false sense of confidence in the prototype. They can mask real-world issues such as network latency and unexpected data formats, leading to potential problems later in development. A better alternative is to incorporate a minimal backend or at least test with a simulated API that closely mimics real behavior; this will provide a more accurate validation of our assumptions and highlight any edge cases we need to address.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Mocked responses hide the real cost of network variability—latency spikes, partial failures, and rate limits will bite us when the proxy hits real APIs. A better alternative is to run the prototype against a *controlled* real backend (even a thin one) to surface these issues early; settle the argument by measuring actual load time and error rates in the same environment we’ll ship to.
